Hey @wannacfuture just so that you are aware, a payment permit can only be generated once per issue. So generally when an issue is re-opened, that means the previous bounty hunter is obligated to fix it without additional compensation (i.e. do a "hotfix") Basically we're calling issues-of-issues "meta issues" https://github.com/ubiquity/ubiquibot/issues/322 is an example of a meta issue. You can see that it has "2 tasks" The way that they are created is by creating a checklist in the original issue comment. A user can mouse-over each list item and immediately convert them into a new issue, which is associated with the meta issue.

https://gnosisscan.io/tx/0xa27fe5d0d3a1d8db5467005fd6ad47dd4eab63dbb52bb9ff9149d1021018cb6c

### Context
It's fast and easy to write todo lists in the original comment of a GitHub issue, and then immediately convert them to "child issues" directly from the GitHub user interface.
The problem I am seeing is that the bounty system breaks down where contributors can "double dip" on rewards easily by claiming bounties for the actual bounties (child issues) and then the "meta" or "parent" issue.
The argument possibly could be made for project management. However in the future all of the **issue creators**, and **commenters** (both are how the project manager would "manage") are to receive compensation for their contributions upon the completion of the bounty.
### Proposal
- When changing a label, the bot should check if there are linked issues in the original comment and disable setting a price (and most importantly, as a consequence, payment permit generation.)
- The bot should comment explaining why it refuses to set a price.
---
              Parent issues should not have bounties. Instead, the child issues should have bounties.
_Originally posted by @pavlovcik in https://github.com/ubiquity/grants/issues/5#issuecomment-1519067539_
